Lighthouses often have distinctive color patterns or architectural styles to help sailors identify their location.
Most lighthouses are equipped with powerful lamps and Fresnel lenses to maximize light visibility over long distances.
Historically, lighthouse keepers lived on-site to maintain the light and signal fog horns during adverse weather conditions.
